editorial.headline: Pharmaceutical Packing, Read Through Bali’s Risk Lens
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers contract or fee-based packing for pharmaceutical materials and medicines, with national foreign ownership open to 100%.
editorial.body:
Pharmaceutical packing is a specialised service activity: packing pharmaceutical materials and finished medicines for a fee or under contract, whether the work is automated or manual. Its scope extends from bottling pharmaceutical liquids to packing solid materials and products in blister packs or aluminium foil, alongside secure medicine packaging, labelling, stamping, sterilisation and related packing work. The focus is the packing operation itself—an activity defined by the careful preparation, protection and presentation of pharmaceutical materials and products.

Every listed business scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—remains open to the activity. That breadth matters because the work can be organised at very different operating sizes while remaining within the same stated scope: handling liquid pharmaceutical products, solid formats, secure packaging and the associated finishing steps. Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%, under the cited Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021 framework. There is no partial foreign-ownership ceiling to read between the lines here: the recorded national ceiling is 100%.

Bali calls for a more precise reading, without warranting pessimism. This activity is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali. The province’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. For this activity at the Besar scale, however, the OSS risk classification is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The record therefore places its Bali status at OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and states that it is not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms, the national openness remains meaningful in Bali for the stated activity: the province’s blanket restriction does not catch it at the large-scale risk classification recorded here.

That distinction is the centre of the picture. A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling does not make Bali’s regulatory context irrelevant; Bali’s PMA rule is expressly risk-based. Yet the same record supplies the answer for this activity: its Besar-scale OSS risk level sits above the Low and Medium-Low categories covered by the moratorium. For founders considering pharmaceutical packing, the relevant frame is therefore a fully open national PMA position combined with a Bali outcome that is not blocked by the provincial moratorium.
editorial.pullQuote: For pharmaceutical packing, the national 100% PMA position remains meaningful in Bali because the recorded large-scale risk level is not caught by the moratorium.
